title: KitKatClub Berlin Dress Code - Quick Summary
items: **There is no single KitKat dress code.** The club hosts a different party almost every night, each run by a different organiser, and each organiser publishes its own rule. Across a normal month that is **nine different dress rules for the same rooms**.

**The club's own baseline is one sentence:** "in general, dresscode means: NOT your average everyday life clothing." Fetish, sexy, daring, extravagant and original are all named as welcome. The jeans-and-T-shirt default is the thing being refused.

**Saturday is the strictest, Monday the most forgiving.** CarneBall Bizarre on Saturday states that jeans and sports shoes are forbidden and normal street clothing is out. Electric Monday accepts smart casual and black T-shirts, and bans long-sleeve pullovers.

**Two Fridays contradict each other.** Four Play, on the first Friday, asks you to avoid police, military and other uniforms of authority. GEGEN Gear, the following Friday, opens its list with uniforms and tells you to dress in codes. Check which Friday your trip lands on.

**A ticket is not entry.** The club's own listings say purchasing a ticket does not guarantee entrance and management reserves the right to refuse entry. Tickets and prices are handled by each night's organiser, not by the club.

**Doors open at 20:00 on Friday and Saturday**, not at midnight. The early hours are a deliberate "Come Together" period to shorten the queue. The dress code and the normal entry fee apply from 8pm, so arriving early buys a calmer door, not a discount.

**Phones go away and consent is the house rule.** Some nights state "Strictly NO phones in the club allowed". Touching someone without their agreement, including in passing, is published as grounds for a lifetime ban.

**Getting home depends on the night.** After Friday or Saturday the U8 runs through the night from Heinrich-Heine-Straße, about every 15 minutes at 04:00. After a Monday, Wednesday or Thursday there is no U8 at 03:30 and the N8 night bus covers the gap.
